💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, gift-giving during the holidays is a delicate dance: you want to find the right item that feels thoughtful and cool but also doesn’t kill your budget or feel like something they already own. Our team is passionate about helping people find the right items, from hosting gifts to products you can bring to your next white elephant to even what to put in your family’s stocking stuffers. The topic we’re tackling? Best gifts under $25 that don’t feel tacky or cheap.

Recent findings suggest that if you dig hard enough, there are actually plenty of unique, thoughtful, and fun finds for under this price point. Whether it be a martini-shaped candle, colorful oven mitts, or a deck of tarot cards, the variety of gift ideas ahead will work for your groups’ gifting needs. These nifty finds are proof that you can buy something that feels special without spending a ton. We’ll raise a glass to that.

For the person who always orders a martini, gift them this candle that nods to a dirty martini! It has notes of greens, herbs, and juniper to make their home smell fresh. However, they may not even burn it, to keep the wax intact for maximum cuteness on the table.

The sentimentalist in your life will appreciate a framed photo, especially if they’re moving away, just moved into a new home, or have been talking about filling their space with meaningful items.

In a recent development, bedding and towel brand Hommey recently launched tableware, and the pieces are just as colorful and fun as their sheets. We love these two-toned bowls, perfect for olives, nuts, and other small snacks for gatherings.

Industry observers note that store-bought lighters aren’t the prettiest, so give them a case to hold their lighter in. This option from Etsy can be personalized, and we’re guessing they’ll want to proudly leave it out on their coffee table right next to their candle.

Everyone talks about their coffee setup, but can we take a moment to talk about a proper matcha setup? Their morning ritual at home isn’t complete without a fun bowl and whisk stand set, and this Anthro pairing comes in many colorful options.

According to recent reports, with winter heading our way, a heated blanket is a must. This soft flannel option comes in a classic plaid pattern that oozes holiday vibes and has 10 adjustable heat settings ranging from 86°F to 122°F.

According to recent reports, if you catch them watching tarot readings on TikTok and YouTube, you know it’s time to get their own deck. This one is perfect for beginners because it comes with thought starters and features cat illustrations for a lighthearted touch.

Whether they just moved into their first apartment or recently invested in an espresso machine, they will need espresso cups. We love this set because it comes with six earthy shades, so if they have a few guests over, everyone has a cup.

Not only does a pie bird look adorable in the middle of a piping-hot apple pie, but it makes it taste better too. Pie birds (or whistles) vent steam during the baking process, preventing the filling from boiling over and the crust from getting soggy.

It has been revealed that we had to test this mini water bottle ourselves, and we found it's incredibly handy to take on the go. It's just the right size to fit in a pocket, holding your morning coffee or a drink for the beach.

Recent findings suggest that for the friend who loves a vinyl dig or a new pressing of their favorite artist, help them keep their collection in tip-top shape. This cleaning kit stores easily in a record cabinet, and keeps even the dustiest records sounding brand-new.

Sources indicate that to fill your latest taper candle holders (and support a small business in the process), snag a set of these hand-poured beeswax taper candles. They add instant drama, and they're paraffin-free. Plus, they're unscented, so they won't clash with the scentscape of your home.

It has been revealed that art therapy can be a great way to release stress and celebrate your inner child. This takes that joy on the road, with a brush that you only need water to use, and a design that disappears over time. No mess, and no requirement to get every stroke perfect.

Fluted designs are back in, and this adorable vase is perfect to display a few choice blooms. The U-shaped design also works as standalone decor, if you just want it to be a striking sculpture.

Recent findings suggest that though this giant farfalle looks like the real thing, it actually smells more like a traditional candle, with notes of jasmine, neroli, and orange blossom. It also comes in a rigatoni shape, if that's more the recipient's thing.

Of course, you can gift a loved one a candle and a set of matches from the drugstore, but that's hardly any fun. Instead, grab a much more stylish version of the traditional matchbox that they can leave out on display. Worry not; there's a striker on the bottom. The matches, however, are not included!

Anyone on your list who appreciates the kitschier things in life will adore this ceramic soap dish shaped like a claw-foot bathtub. Just like an actual tub, there is a tiny hole for drainage so that the suds don't sit (and get moldy) in the basin.

Industry observers note that as far as we're concerned, no one can ever have too many oven mitts. After all, they get stained rapidly, so having a fresh, clean pair on hand is always a good idea.

Recent findings suggest that there's no shame in being afraid of the dark, so we say embrace the fear and snag this charming (and portable) touch lamp. It gets brighter and dimmer with just the tap of a finger. It almost mimics candlelight, but unlike a flickering flame, it is safe to use all night.

Sources indicate that it may be hard to believe that something so artistic is from Amazon, the place we buy our sponges, gym socks, and YETI water bottles, but here we are. You can rest assured that, unlike some of the other goods you may buy on Amazon, this bowl is not made in bulk. In fact, it's from one of the thousands of small businesses that sell their wares on the platform. How's that for a lucky find?

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In a recent development, based on Frederick Forsyth’s bestselling 1971 thriller, the Sky and Peacock series—starring Eddie Redmayne as the world’s most elusive assassin—earned much acclaim when it arrived in 2024.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

With James Bond back in the headlines—at long last, we finally have our 007, even if a certain crowd is upset about it—The Day of the Jackal is also gearing up for a return.

In a recent development, based on Frederick Forsyth’s bestselling 1971 thriller, the Sky and Peacock series—starring Eddie Redmayne as the world’s most elusive assassin—earned much acclaim when it arrived in 2024. Now the British actor is reprising the role in a second season arriving next March.

Peacock has just released a first-look teaser, taken from the opening of the new series. Plot details are being kept under wraps for now, but the Jackal is back in action, and there should be plenty of globetrotting, elaborate schemes, and unfortunate encounters for anyone who gets in his way.

You can watch the full teaser below.

Sources indicate that if the first season of The Day of the Jackal is anything to go by, Peacock has another hit on its hands. After its first 75 days on streaming, NBCUniversal reported that it was the most-watched fresh original drama series ever recorded on Peacock. Plus, Redmayne earned Golden Globe, Critics’ Choice and SAG Award nominations for his performance.

Redmayne won’t be the only familiar face returning. Úrsula Corberó, Charles Dance and Chukwudi Iwuji are also back, while Matt Bomer, Pablo Schreiber, Weruche Opia and Pia Tjelta join the cast. That’s quite a few new faces for the Jackal to get acquainted with.

The Day of the Jackal season 2 arrives on Peacock in March 2027.

Mckenna Grace Is Winning the Method Dressing Hunger Games

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1298 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cosmopolitan

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, method dressing for press tours is part of the reason 2026’s year of movies feels so unstoppable.
  • “Mckenna was absolutely certain from the beginning that she wanted to embrace method dressing for this press tour, and I was completely on board,” Molly tells Cosmopolitan.
  • According to recent reports, the concept of method dressing isn’t fresh, but it’s been incredibly impactful on movie press runs in particular over the past few years.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, method dressing for press tours is part of the reason 2026’s year of movies feels so unstoppable. The carpets for the latest Hunger Games film, Sunrise on the Reaping, have been heating up look after look, but no one is catching fire quite like Mckenna Grace. Along with her stylist, Molly Dickson, the pair have been turning out absolute masterpieces, with extraordinary commitment to Hunger Games literary lore: As small as ladybugs in Mckenna’s hair (a nod to the ‘Ladybug, Ladybug’ song Haymitch Abernathy sings to Maysilee Donner in Sunrise on the Reaping) to step out in NYC, and as large as a recreation of Katniss’s truly iconic wedding dress from The Hunger Games 2: Catching Fire.

“Mckenna was absolutely certain from the beginning that she wanted to embrace method dressing for this press tour, and I was completely on board,” Molly tells Cosmopolitan.

According to recent reports, the concept of method dressing isn’t fresh, but it’s been incredibly impactful on movie press runs in particular over the past few years. In practice, actors wear looks that reference niche details of the films they’re promoting. Think Zendaya’s Greek-goddess-forward looks for The Odyssey, Margot Robbie’s Barbie ensembles pulled straight from the dolls themselves, Ariana Grande and Cynthia Erivo in a lifetime’s worth of pink and green for Wicked.

Sources indicate that “I think the best method dressing moments are the ones that tell a story, while still feeling like incredible fashion looks of their own,” states Molly. “We wanted the fans to have those moments of recognition and excitement, but we also wanted someone who knew nothing about The Hunger Games to look at Mckenna and simply think she looked incredible!”.

So how did they do it? What references were on their mood board? What dress almost never saw the light of day? And most importantly: What’s the story behind THE legendary arena dress from the UK premiere? Superstar stylist Molly Dickson answers our most pressing press tour related questions.

In a recent development, it was a really collaborative process between the two of us. Mckenna would come to me with ideas, and I would figure out how to translate them into fashion. She was the one who said, ‘Ladybugs are part of the movie, we need to do a ladybug look!’ From there, I started sourcing pieces that either incorporated ladybugs directly or finding more unexpected, interesting ways to reference them.

In a recent development, we were very intentional about making sure every look had a connection to some part of the Hunger Games universe. We wanted the references to feel thoughtful and recognizable to the fans, while still creating beautiful fashion moments that felt authentic to Mckenna and her personal style.

I don't think either of us initially realized just how invested the Hunger Games fans would be in all the little references and Easter eggs! Once we started seeing that reaction, it became more fun to dig deeper into the franchise and pull inspiration from different characters and iconic moments. Mckenna knows this world so well, and I loved being able to bring her ideas to life.

Mckenna really wanted to pay homage to the strong female characters throughout the franchise—specifically Katniss and Joanna Mason—which became the inspiration for so many of our looks. As we started fittings, we found ways to incorporate inspiration from Rue as well.

In a recent development, we wanted a mix of more recognizable references and subtle nods rather than exact recreations of costumes from the movies. We used the original costumes and characters as our starting point, but then put our own fashion interpretation on them. I think that's where my creativity really comes in. You want fans to recognize the inspiration, but you also want the looks to feel fresh, elevated, and true to the person wearing them.

Sources indicate that I really can't think of a better way to generate excitement and conversation around a movie through fashion than method dressing. It's such a fun way to bring the story beyond the screen, and give fans something deeper to connect with. What I loved most about this tour was seeing the conversations happening online, not just about the fashion itself, but about the characters, the references, and ultimately the film.

I think my personal favorite was Mckenna’s Paris look inspired by Katniss's wedding gown. It was such a major fashion moment—we actually went back and forth on whether it might be too much! Mckenna’s team really encouraged us to go for it, and they were absolutely right.

The most challenging part was figuring out how to recreate the sculptural silver elements. Michael Ngo made experimental custom silver pieces for us, which we paired with a beautiful vintage Monique Lhuillier wedding gown. I loved that the complete look felt like a true tribute to Katniss's iconic gown, but still had its own fashion identity. It was one of those moments where the creativity, collaboration, and a little bit of risk-taking really paid off!

Sources indicate that we really wanted to pay homage to the strong female characters throughout the Hunger Games franchise while still staying true to Mckenna's personal style. We wanted each look to tell a story and have a connection to the films, but never feel like she was wearing a costume.

For the press junkets and more casual appearances, we focused on subtle nods to the movies, whether that was through color, texture, or small details that fans might recognize. For the bigger red carpet moments, we had the opportunity to be a little more dramatic and lean into those bigger, more established references. The fun of this tour was finding that balance between fashion and storytelling!

Honestly, I have to give all the credit to Mckenna’s mom for this one! She actually discovered the dress on Instagram and sent it over to me. The brand is ALmée, and they’re based in Vietnam.

I love that this look came together in such an unexpected way. It wasn't something we had custom-designed or planned months in advance. It was really just Mckenna's mom spotting something incredible and all of us realizing how perfectly it fit into the Hunger Games world.

That's one of my favorite things about styling: Sometimes the most exciting looks come from the most unexpected places, and this was definitely one of those moments!

It has been revealed that one of the looks I was most excited about, but also the most stumped on creatively, Katniss's iconic Girl on Fire gown. The challenge was figuring out how to translate that moment into something that felt like a beautiful red carpet gown rather than a costume.

Recent findings suggest that cong Tri immediately came to mind because of their intricate beadwork and craftsmanship. I knew I wanted the fire gown to incorporate beading because of the way it catches the light, especially under red carpet lighting and camera flashes. I felt that was going to be key to creating the illusion of flames and bringing the dress to life.

It was honestly the perfect collaboration. The Cong Tri team was so willing to push the design creatively. After experimenting with different fabrics, textures, and techniques, the end result was exactly what we had hoped for. The dress felt dramatic and powerful, with that obvious nod to Katniss, but still felt like a really beautiful fashion moment. That's always the goal with these kinds of looks!

Ali Royals loves true stories and hates writing in the third person, even though she’s doing it right now. Ali is a poet, writer, and denier of any Carrie Bradshaw allegations. Follow her on Instagram and Substack for her daily Outfit Prompts, where she tells herself stories in order to get dressed.

Ella Langley and Tucker Wetmore’s Full Relationship Timeline

📅 30 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (431 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ella Langley and Tucker Wetmore are country music’s newest couple.
  • After months of speculation about their relationship, multiple sources confirmed to People on Sept.
  • Recent findings suggest that neither Langley nor Wetmore has publicly commented on their relationship yet.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ella Langley and Tucker Wetmore are country music’s newest couple.

After months of speculation about their relationship, multiple sources confirmed to People on Sept. 23, 2026, that Langley and Wetmore are dating. The news came one day after the two country singers attended the Nashville Songwriter Awards, where Langley celebrated another major moment in her career.

Recent findings suggest that neither Langley nor Wetmore has publicly commented on their relationship yet. But their history goes back to at least late 2025, when they began appearing at some of the same industry events before sparking dating rumors during a trip to the British Virgin Islands that December. Since then, they’ve also shared the stage.

Below, a full timeline of everything we know about Langley and Wetmore’s relationship so far.

Langley and Wetmore were both at the BMI Country Awards in Nashville on November 18. The two appeared together in a group photo from the event.

At the time, neither had publicly suggested that they were romantically involved.

Dating speculation began the following month after Langley and Wetmore were photographed together at the Soggy Dollar Bar in the British Virgin Islands.

Langley and Wetmore reunited onstage on March 10 at the Heart Strings for Hope charity event.

During the event, Langley joined Wetmore for an acoustic performance of his song “Sunburn.” The two sat across from each other with their guitars as they performed the track together.

On September 22, Langley and Wetmore both attended the ninth annual Nashville Songwriter Awards at Nashville’s Ryman Auditorium.

It was a particularly big night for Langley: “Choosin’ Texas” won Song of the Year at the ceremony.

After the awards, Langley and Wetmore were photographed leaving the Ryman together through a side door.

Industry observers note that the following day, multiple sources confirmed to People that the two are dating. Neither Langley nor Wetmore has spoken about the relationship themselves.

In a recent development, langley and Wetmore appeared to take another trip to the Virgin Islands together. A man dining at a restaurant they went to posted a video of them arriving.

On November 18, Wetmore was asked about his rumored relationship with Langley while attending the 2026 CMA Awards in Nashville.

When People asked who he was cheering for that evening, Wetmore avoided mentioning Langley, instead naming two male country artists.

“Zach Top or Stephen Wilson Jr.,” he joked.

“I freaking love that guy. Both of them,” he added with a laugh.

Langley entered the ceremony with nine nominations, the most of any artist that year. She went home with six awards.

APC Just Dropped a Pair of Incredibly Clean Casios

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (451 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that we’re in a great era for affordable fashion-collab watches.
  • The first collaboration between the two brands saw them rework the hallowed A1000 digital-display watch.
  • It has been revealed that what about the APC-ness of it all?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that we’re in a great era for affordable fashion-collab watches. Timex is leading the way: its link-ups with Noah, Todd Snyder, and J. Crew are masterclasses in adding personality to classic designs without going OTT. But don’t count Casio out of the race. The Japanese giant has just followed up its 2024 collab with APC. The pair are perfectly matched: Casio watches are known for being beautifully functional and understated—adjectives that fit APC’s spartan aesthetic too.

The first collaboration between the two brands saw them rework the hallowed A1000 digital-display watch. That release stripped back a lot of the original’s markings and added the APC logo on the dial. This time around, it's the AQ-240 getting a makeover. The case is squarer than the rectangular A1000, and while there’s a narrow window for a digital display, the watch maintains the traditional analog format with hands and hour markers. Here, you get the best of both worlds. The watch is sold out on APC's website but still available through Casio, so act fast if you want one. The silver variant is $110, and the gold goes for $135.

It has been revealed that what about the APC-ness of it all? That part is the opposite of loud: as with the previous collab, there isn’t much giving away the brand's participation. We’ve got the APC logo on the dial and the buckle, plus the brand’s guitar-and-dagger insignia engraved out of sight on the caseback. Casio already offers the regular A1000 in a bunch of different colorways, but these two latest ones are made specifically for the APC collab. The release includes a silver case with a dark-green dial and another in gold on gold. Both of the pieces have a brushed sun-ray effect on the dial. The vibe is refined and stripped back; this is a fashion watch that almost feels anti-fashion.

It has been revealed that maybe the best way to think about it is as the reverse side of the coin to the excellent newly introduced G-Shock 2500 Series. Both come from Casio, and both are minimal and functional. But the G-Shocks are major and bulky, with a design that seems to tip its hat to Patek Philippe’s Nautilus. These new ones are slim and nearly dressy. Put the two new releases together, and you’ve got pretty much all bases covered. And if those aforementioned Timex collabs felt a bit too classicist for you, then the Casio-APC partnership takes things in a more modern direction. Far from just being a cash grab, the “fashion watch” is now one of the best routes into affordable, on-point horology.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that A new season of The Circle is here, but it’s not just civilians competing this time around. In the Hulu revival series, celebrities are also part of the competition, including The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star Layla Taylor—though her fellow competitors don’t know that, since she’s playing as a former Mormon bisexual bro named Doug. She’s not doing it alone, either, as she entered the Circle with her bestie Kate Racker. Who is Kate, you ask? I paid a visit to her and Layla’s apartment in Atlanta to get to know her (and her SLOMW lore) a little better.

Sources indicate that as you might recall, Kate was first introduced during SLOMW season 2 as Chase McWhorter’s on-again, off-again girlfriend. She later explained to People that she and Chase met just three weeks after she split from her ex-husband (with whom she shares a son, Rowan), and it was through Chase that she met the MomTok crew, including Layla (though fun fact: Kate already knew Jessi Draper, who was her neighbor growing up, as well as Jacob Neeley, who she used to work with in private equity).

Sources indicate that it wasn’t until summer 2025, however, that Layla and Kate really cemented their friendship. “Before she started dating Mason [McWhorter], and I was kind of off with Chase, Layla and I were just single together. So we’d go out, we talk every day,” Kate previously told People. “We were kind of each other’s person. We’d FaceTime 24/7 and just got really, really, really close.”.

It has been revealed that now they’re spending 24/7 together in the Circle, where—according to Kate—they’ve only gotten into “one tiny little tiff” so far. “We are sisters at this point, and I consider her my sister,” she indicates, adding, “I think the thing about me and Layla is we’re both like pretty sensitive, but we both love each other so much, and we’re committed [to winning]. Like, I have goosebumps.”.

My substantial question for them: Why did they decide to step into the Circle as a catfish rather than themselves?

“It’s kind of fun to like step into somebody that you’re not,” Layla indicates.

It has been revealed that kate agrees, adding, “It’s a new experience. I mean, we’re all about new experiences and trying new things and role play. We love role play. We’ll try anything three times.”.

In a recent development, and if you’re wondering whether they have a certain man (or a certain pair of brothers) in mind while playing “Doug,” the answer is...not really. “I feel like he’s kind of a collection of the men that we have encountered in our life or even dated in the past,” explains Layla. “Like, all of them.”.

“I think we’re trying to lean into the douchebag,” adds Kate. “Not to say all men are douchebags, but no, there’s some great ones. Or, you know, a few.”.

It has been revealed that layla then clarifies, “We’re not men haters. No, not at all. We are men observers. And we’ve observed poor behavior from the men that we do know, and we’re just emulating and dramatizing that.”.

I also ask Layla if she’s missing her girlfriend Kelsie Chesser while she’s in the Circle, and she notes that—while she says, “For sure, you know, I love her dearly”—the harder part is being away from her kids. “Yeah, we both cry every day,” Layla says. “Cried myself to sleep last night. But Kate is my bestie, and there’s no one I’d rather be trapped in here with.”.

Since there are players who have yet to be revealed in the Circle, I need to know: Which of the Mormon Wives would they be most excited to see pop up on their screen?

It has been revealed that “I would love to see Jessi,” Kate indicates. “Obviously, Miranda [Hope]. Miranda would be great. Mayci [Neeley]. Like, any of them.”.

Layla grins before adding, “Yeah, I think I can say everyone...but one.”.

“She is getting to know him,” the source added. “Kylie is having fun. After years of back and forth with Travis [Scott, her ex-boyfriend and father of her two children], she just wants to date without any pressure.”.

Industry observers note that in May, a source told Entertainment Tonight that the latest couple was trying to keep things quiet. They're “casually seeing each other but are trying to keep it low-key,” the source stated.

Take Note: This Is How Cool People Are Decorating for Thanksgiving This Year

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 12 min read (2477 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

⏱️ ~12 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Every item on this page was hand-picked by a House Beautiful editor.
  • According to recent reports, pumpkin centerpieces, rustic garlands, dried-fruit wreaths, and cornucopias are classic Thanksgiving decorations.
  • From traditional touches to wholly unexpected looks, read on to see how they’re making their homes feel festive this autumn, and maybe you’ll be inspired to try something fresh this year.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Every item on this page was hand-picked by a House Beautiful editor. We may earn commission on some of the items you choose to buy.

According to recent reports, pumpkin centerpieces, rustic garlands, dried-fruit wreaths, and cornucopias are classic Thanksgiving decorations. They’re timeless and beloved, but they can also feel predictable. Traditional decor has its place, of course, but Thanksgiving tablescapes—and dinner parties in general—are evolving, much like interiors, to feel more personal, lived-in, and layered. So we asked nine tastemakers and experts how they’re decorating for this family-centric holiday.

From traditional touches to wholly unexpected looks, read on to see how they’re making their homes feel festive this autumn, and maybe you’ll be inspired to try something fresh this year.

Ever since designer Mikel Welch moved to sunny California, his family has never hesitated to go to his for Thanksgiving to escape the chilly Michigan weather. It’s become a tradition to gather at his house, and similarly to how he grew up, Welch likes to keep his decorations for the holiday understated and warm.

“I love getting the exterior of my house into full fall mode with mums, pumpkins, and seasonal greenery,” Welch tells House Beautiful. “The beauty of fall decorating is that it can carry you from October straight through Thanksgiving without having to change much.”.

The designer’s house is filled with dark, moody colors and earthy textures year-round, so he focuses mainly on bringing natural elements inside to do the work for him. “I also have a little tradition with my dad,” he adds. “For the past couple of years, we've made trips to the nursery together to pick out flowers, greenery, and sometimes bales of hay for the front of the house. It's become something I really enjoy doing with him.”.

“Thanksgiving has always been a substantial family affair,” real estate expert and maximalism extraordinaire Harvin Greene notes. She’s happy to keep that tradition going as an adult, just in her own way. In the past, Greene’s aunt and uncle would have everyone at their house for the big meal, but last year, they passed the hosting baton to Greene for the first time. “I may have gotten a little carried away...in the best possible way.”.

According to recent reports, getting to decorate two tables—one for the “adults,” another for the “kids,” even though they’re technically all grown-ups, too—Greene used this opportunity to design two completely different tablescapes. “I grew up surrounded by women who understood that a beautifully set table and a genuinely good time should go hand in hand,” she adds.

Industry observers note that the one in the formal dining space (i.e., the “adults’” table) was theatrical and dramatic, and nearly everything on it had some sort of familial connection, from her parents’ engraved goblets to her husband’s grandmother’s sterling flatware. The kids’ table, on the other hand, was whimsical and vibrant, complete with a yellow patterned tablecloth, colorful glassware, and playful animal candlesticks. “I don't feel the need to follow the traditional Thanksgiving color palette,” Greene claims. “Who decided Thanksgiving had to be orange and brown? Yellow, pink, turquoise, and green can be just as festive.”.

The holiday isn’t over until they bring out the Bingo cards, a spirited Thanksgiving tradition that Greene’s Aunt Jean started—which involves cash prizes. “It's one of those family traditions that makes the holiday feel like ours, no matter whose house we're celebrating in.”.

Industry observers note that talia Hubble is no stranger to a good dinner party—much of her content actually centers around her love of hosting. But Thanksgiving is a bit extra special for the Rhode Islander, especially since it’s being held at her cottage this year. “Growing up, it was just me and my mom, and she was too busy to decorate,” Hubble indicates. “I think that’s part of why I’ve fallen in love with seasonal decorating as an adult, I get to bring all my cozy childhood decorating dreams to life!”.

In a recent development, as soon as the calendar switches from October to November, Hubble starts decorating for fall, opting for an eclectic mix of subtle Christmas decor (think bows, garlands, and wreaths), an excessive amount of taper candles, and a traditional Thanksgiving palette of oranges, browns, greens, and reds. Every year looks a little bit different, but there are pieces in her collection that are simply too cute not to bring out every holiday season.

Sources indicate that “Half the fun of pulling everything out for Thanksgiving is remembering where it came from,” she claims. “I think the best decor is a culmination of pieces you’ve been collecting for years, and the memories behind those pieces are what make the table feel special and uniquely yours.”.

By the time she’s done decorating, her home feels like a warm, welcoming escape, somewhere her guests can exhale. “My philosophy is that you can’t go wrong when you aim for cozy, colorful, and embrace a little organized mess,” Hubble adds. “My favorite Thanksgiving tables are the ones that look even better halfway through dinner, when the napkins are rumpled and everyone’s reaching for seconds.”.

Chef and food stylist Romilly Newman can’t always count on being in the same place as her family for Thanksgiving since everyone’s scattered about, but she always makes a point to throw an autumnal dinner with friends around the holiday time, complete with beautiful fall decor.

It has been revealed that her mom never decorated their home while she was growing up with specific Thanksgiving decorations—instead, she would decorate with deep orange and red flowers to capture the fall vibe. Newman’s style as an adult is similar. “I am fall-obsessed, so as soon as the temperature drops from summer, I'm setting up branches, candles, and darker accents,” she says. “I love the atmosphere inside and outside around Thanksgiving time, and I try my best to bottle that up in my home.”.

Natural thicker linen, pops of silver, dark florals, and moody lighting envelop her space as the chef relies mostly on candlelight and organic elements—like figs, sage, chestnuts, and mandarins—as the decorative accents.

Recent findings suggest that “Thanksgiving is great because it brings family together and offers time to enjoy food, friends, and being at home,” Newman adds. “Whatever your style is, try to create an environment that allows for great conversation and a festive evening. You want everyone to be comfortable and feel the holiday spirit.”.

Recent findings suggest that when writer Olivia Noceda was a child, she would stay up late the night before Thanksgiving and design custom menus for everyone on Microsoft Paint, which she would then print out, frame, and place on each table setting in preparation for the significant meal. The holiday was a big deal for Noceda’s mother, who would always put on the most beautiful Thanksgiving gatherings. “I think that's where my love for hosting and setting a beautiful table really started,” she explains.

However, for the last six years, Noceda has been having Thanksgiving with her husband’s side of the family, so when she does host around the holiday, it’s typically for Friendsgiving. “I don't necessarily pick a theme, but I do like everything to feel cohesive,” she explains of her decorating process. “I usually start incorporating little autumnal touches sometime in October and let them carry me through Thanksgiving.”.

The writer and recipe developer lets the season guide her, building her tablescape and decor around a beautiful branch from the farmers’ market, a bowl of pears or persimmons, a collection of little pumpkins and squash, or a few taper candles on the dining room table. Ingredients play a major part in her decor—she can even take a fresh loaf of bread and make it feel special on her table.

In a recent development, for the rest of her decor, she likes to incorporate vintage serving pieces, everyday elements, and elevated details like antique silver and linen napkins with things she already owns to lean into that lived-in, warm feeling. The last thing she wants is her home to feel like a department store display. “Nothing needs to match perfectly, and I actually prefer when it doesn't,” Noceda adds.

According to recent reports, what entrepreneur and Real Housewives of New York star Erin Lichy remembers best about Thanksgivings growing up is the smell. “We always spent Thanksgiving out east, and the house was full of pumpkins, local hay, and lanterns,” she explains. The scent of that fresh produce, mixed with her grandmother’s homemade turkey t’bit, has shaped the way she decorates for and hosts Thanksgiving. “That coveted and highly personal (and incredibly delicious) recipe is in my cookbook, She’s a Host, and it’s part of every Thanksgiving I host.”.

In a recent development, decorating starts in the kitchen for her family. Lichy wants the home to smell like fall, so she focuses on that sense, making seasonal recipes with squash and pumpkin and incorporating autumnal flowers in her interiors. The melding of those scents gives her townhouse a warm feeling, especially when mixed with layered fall colors and the crackling of the fireplace.

Ever since Lichy and her family have moved into their townhouse, she’s been obsessed with decorating her stoop too. “The stoop is the first thing everyone sees, so this year I decided to bring in Simon Wallace Design to make it really stand out!” Lichy adds. “They completely transformed it with layers of seasonal color and texture, and it feels so warm and welcoming.” She specifically loves using the faux garlands and pinecones, as well as lanterns, from Balsam Hill and Frontgate because they’re so beautifully made that they look real, and she’s able to reuse them year after year.

No matter what she does to decorate though, she just wants her home to feel warm and lived-in, and this is the season and holiday to really lean into that.

Sources indicate that decorating for the holidays is Gabby Amato’s version of a self-care day. “It's truly one of my favorite days of the year,” she says. “I carve out a weekend afternoon when my husband and son are out of the house, light my favorite fall candles, turn on some music, and have the house entirely to myself.”.

Amato, the founder of Table Two Studio, a paper plate brand which specializes in beautiful, artistic designs that you definitely won’t want to throw away, credits her love of Thanksgiving and the fall season in general to her mother. While growing up in the ‘90s, she saw her mom put so much care and effort into the holiday decorations, always making their home feel warm, nostalgic, and full of spirit. “For Thanksgiving, she decorated our mantel with gourds, greenery, and ceramic pilgrim statues that were a gift from my grandmother,” Amato states. “We had oversized cornstalks and pumpkins at the front door. Nothing ever felt overly styled or precious.”.

It’s this feeling that has stuck with her throughout her life, and it’s what she hopes she captures in her own home every year. She begins decorating for the fall early, right after Labor Day, pulling out old pieces and unboxing anything latest and arranging it all in fresh ways so nothing feels stale. “I love beautiful decor, of course, but I'm much more interested in creating an atmosphere than achieving a particular aesthetic,” she adds. “I want my home to feel warm, lived-in, a little nostalgic, and festive.”.

Donna Lennard’s family was never one for holiday dressing—most of the attention at Thanksgiving fell on the delicious food shared with family. As a restauranteur and cofounder of beloved NYC establishment il Buco, it makes sense why the meal remains to be the most important thing to Lennard even today.

“Clearly, the table is always festive, whether it’s the tablecloth, the napkins, or linens that reflect the season in burnt orange and the like,” she explains. “I love to decorate a table with assorted colorful gourds and seasonal florals, beautiful candlelight (our beeswax candles already have an orange glow), orange ranunculus, and the occasional dried floral.” Colorful Pienza glassware dots the table and her plethora of beautiful tableware gives it more character, but she keeps everything else relatively simple to ensure the food remains the center of attention.

Though Lennard doesn’t often host her family and friends for the Thanksgiving meal, she’s already looking forward to next year when everyone will finally gather at her beach house.

In a recent development, being from Australia, Kendall Knox—the cofounder of Olive Ateliers along with her husband—didn’t have a personal reference of what the holiday “should” be or look like. This gives her the freedom of deciding what it is for her family. “What it has become is an intimate table: my husband Ben, our son Rhodes, and Ben's mum,” she says. “No rotation, no kids' table, no forty-pound bird. Just the four of us and a dinner that runs long because nobody is in a hurry to leave it.”.

It has been revealed that since Knox isn’t beholden to the classic Thanksgiving decor, she tends to keep her home and her table rather simple, “shopping the house,” as she puts it to decorate instead of buying something upcoming. She keeps a rather neutral palette of rich browns, creamy whites, terracotta, and silver, then uses antique linens, mismatched silverware, and candlesticks that have collected wax to capture the true lived-in feel.

It has been revealed that her focus tends to be on the table and the meal, letting the food add more color. If a tablecloth has a wine ring on it from the year before, all the better—it complements the stacked plates at the end of the meal.

“The objects that come out every year, that get a little more marked each time, are the ones that end up meaning the most,” Knox adds. “Thanksgiving is just a very good excuse to use them.”.

Are You a Super Ager? This Competition Will Be the Judge of That

💡 Key Takeaways

  • As soon as the volunteer says “go” he sprints to the box, plants his hands, and hoists his feet up and over.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that alan Krepack stands with his hands on his hips and takes a deep breath as he sizes up the Over Under: an obstacle with a high wooden box and low wooden beam spread 10 meters apart. Music booms over the speakers and other competitors shuffle around the cavernous room of the Armory Track in Washington Heights, Newly introduced York, but Krepack stays laser-focused, thanks to years of meditation practice.

As soon as the volunteer says “go” he sprints to the box, plants his hands, and hoists his feet up and over. As he lands on the other side, he sprints to the beam, dropping down into an army crawl. “Take your time, take your time,” his son yells from the sidelines. Krepack reaches the far end, rushes back, and repeats the sequence again before crossing the line in 51 seconds. To cool down, he paces back and forth with his hands on his head. “I think I’m a sprinter, I’m a jumper, but then it’s like, fuck, no, I’m 73 years old,” he says, catching his breath.

The challenge is just the first of eight trials Krepeck will tackle throughout the day alongside his sons, Harrison and Aaron, at the Super Age Games, a fitness and mental competition designed to assess abilities associated with healthy aging. On November 7th, the inaugural day-long event drew 530 athletes from 42 states and 15 countries, and about 70% of participants were between the ages of 40 and 64. Krepeck agreed to let me shadow him to understand this newly introduced event through the lens of someone who is, in fact, aging, and would like to do so gracefully.

Industry observers note that the name of the Games comes from a buzzword that originated in the longevity world: super ager. The term was originally coined by Northwestern University researchers to describe adults over 80 whose memories rival those of people 30 years younger. These days it’s thrown around on podcasts and in books to describe anyone who defies both the typical trajectory of both cognitive and physical aging.

The inaugural Super Age Games drew 530 athletes from 42 states and 15 countries.

According to recent reports, from crawling across a cargo net to reading microexpressions, the challenges in the competition measure longevity markers like functional strength, aerobic capacity, balance, and cognitive skill. At the end, athletes see where they rank among their age group and receive their “Super Age,” learning how their body’s physical fitness stacks up against the general U.S. population’s.

In an era where your average middle-aged midwestern dad is training for Hyrox, and a upcoming, outlandishly extreme challenge is being invented every few months, the Super Age games are a low-key counterpoint to raw, stunty, athleticism, born from the metric-obsessed fitness subcultures who prize longevity above all. And now that fitness trackers like Whoop or Apple Watch can track VO2max, heart rate variability, and resting heart rates, that group continues to grow. Along the way, these stats have become status symbols on par with owning a Lamborghini. And now that overall health is quantifiable, fitness values have become less about just how fast you run or how much you lift, but how slowly aging.

In a recent development, it follows that, despite its name, Super Age Games isn’t just for aging athletes. The crowd there leaned middle-aged, and the youngest person at the competition was 21. As we stood by the dead hang station, Krepak pointed across the room at a brolic young man who looked like he could be an NFL prospect: “That dude’s a serious athlete,” he states, as we watched him run around the track cradling a sandbag on his shoulder.

Recent findings suggest that unlike competitions like Hyrox, where athletes race through a sequence of workouts against the clock, the Super Age Games allows competitors to rest as long as they need between trials. In fact, Junior Kennedy, the fitness program director for the Games, encourages it. “There's no rush,” he says. “The goal is to get through each event as intentionally as you can. We need to understand what it means to recover.”.

Each trial was developed with a certain longevity marker in mind, and developed with input from researchers at the Buck Institute for Research on Aging, a leading nonprofit research center based in Novato, California dedicated to understanding aging. The Over Under, for example, tests agility by judging how fast you can change levels and switch directions. Meanwhile, the Synapse, a challenge where participants track moving balls on a screen and identify them after they've been shuffled around, is meant to measure cognitive processing.

Challenges in the competition measure longevity markers like functional strength, aerobic capacity, balance, and cognitive skill.

Industry observers note that krepack, a psychologist and lifelong athlete from Mill Valley, California, first heard about the event through its founder, David Stewart. Stewart is a media founder behind two niche longevity platforms, AGEIST and Super Age, where he writes about longevity, wellness, and redefining aging (one of his website testimonial’s states he has made aging “cool and aspirational.”). Krepack’s generally a skeptic of the profit-driven modern wellness industry—“I've always had a jaded view of all of that stuff,” he says—but he has followed both Stewart and the Buck Institutes’ work for years.

In a recent development, the competition appealed to Krepack, in part because he’s spent decades cultivating a consistent exercise routine he’s proud of. He played baseball in college and has spent much of his life skiing, cycling, and playing other sports. These days, his schedule revolves around a handful of rituals: bike rides on Mondays and Fridays, a Saturday hike with a friend, gardening, yoga, and Zen meditation most days. When he signed up for the Games in June, he altered his exercise routine, lifted more weights, practiced hanging from a bar, and experimented with the Neurotracker cognitive test online.

Yet all that training didn’t prepare Krepack for the biggest surprise of his day. After scoring well on both the Inferno (the assault bike VO2max test) and Synapse, next came the fourth trial: the “Tightrope,” a balance challenge that requires competitors to walk along a low beam while carrying a water-filled bag, taking as many consecutive steps as they can in two minutes without falling. He had expected to excel, thanks to years of skiing and yoga. Instead, he struggled to keep steady as the water shifted inside the bag. As his foot slipped off the bar, his eyes got wide. “I can’t believe my balance,” he says. “That’s my one disappointment in life now.”.

Alan Krepack's sons Harrison and Aaron during the “tightrope” challenge.

Krepack was still hard on himself as we walked over to the dead hang trial. But after beating both his sons’ times, he seemed to get his competitive spirit back. He pushed through the remaining challenge determined to finish strong. And he did: By the end of the Games, he had placed second overall, with scores adjusted for age.

According to recent reports, A few days after the competition, I checked in with Krepack to ask him how he’d processed the event. He responded with screenshots of his scores. His highest score came from the cargo net, which he credited to sheer determination rather than any particular finesse: “due to my will and overcoming an unconventional and desperate style!” he texted me, “Plus my sons were great support and focus partners.”.

But the Games were also a reality check about aging: “I left there feeling both young and old,” he tells me on a phone call. As he watched his sons rocket through the obstacles, he was forced to confront how much of his athleticism he’d lost. “They just flew over it. They were so fluid, and so fast,” he notes. “I’m not 30 or 40 or 50 or 60 anymore.”.

Industry observers note that despite all the longevity industry's promises of maintaining youth, Krepack sees little value in denying the inevitable. Aging well, he notes, is about “accepting, improving, and doing your best. It’s not a denial of who you are at this point in life.” The goal, he says, is to make the most of what you’re still capable of.

Here’s everything Prince Harry stated throughout his appearance on This Morning.

Following the family’s move back to the UK in September earlier this year, Harry shared that the children, Lilibet and Archie, are finally getting British accents having spent most of their childhood so far in California, adding he was “squeezing the accents out of them.”.

He also revealed there was a bit of a “culture shift” for the children when it came to their newly introduced schooling as they now have to wear school uniform, something they didn’t have to do while in school in the U.S.

“I think the kids being in school uniforms is a big change for them,” he explained. “But it has certainly helped. The confidence in both of them has gone through the roof since being in a UK school, which is really, really nice to see.”.

During his chat with Alison and Dermot, the hosts quizzed him on all things UK vs. USA, and Alison asked him for his thoughts on Robert Pattinson being cast as James Bond, to which Prince Harry responded, “I think it’s in great hands.” He also added he couldn’t wait to see the film.

He was also asked whether he preferred EastEnders or Suits (which is the show his wife Meghan Markle is most known for acting in) and he ultimately picked Suits.

Every Friday on This Morning, hosts Dermot and Alison pick a variety of music to play throughout the show, and Harry was also given the chance to pick a song for Friday.

Recent findings suggest that he revealed his choice was “Runnin’ (Lose It All)” by Naughty Boy feat. Beyoncé and Arrow Benjamin, and added it’s the song he listens to while doing a cold plunge.

The Duke of Sussex joined Dermot and Alison for the cooking segment of the series where they were learning how to create a Christmas cake with Phil Vickery.

During the segment, the hosts asked him about whether he liked to bake and he revealed that children Lilibet and Archie liked to bake, but that the whole family was a fan of The Great British Bake Off, which is of course presented by Alison.

Harry added that the series was good this year and he was a big fan of Tom to win the series.

As the cooking segment wound down, Alison asked him who would be doing the cooking at Christmas in his home this year.

He went on to say his wife and mother-in-law were the better cooks in his household and so they would be doing the cooking for the festive season. The Duke also revealed they may do things differently this year and have a Christmas gumbo, too!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that taylor Swift has returned to the Country Music Awards! Last night, the country singer-turned-global superstar, who recently celebrated the 20th anniversary of her debut, self-titled album, went back to her roots with an appearance (and performance) at the 2026 award show.

The Grammy-winning artist was nominated for Single of the Year for her Toy Story 5 track “I Knew It, I Knew You,” and making her grand entrance, she brought a bit of the franchise’s signature yellow to the red carpet.

Her daffodil gown, with its strapless silhouette and voluminous bubble skirt, was courtesy of Oscar de la Renta, a house Swift has long turned to over the years. After the designer passed away in 2014, she called him her “all-time favorite designer” on social media, and attended the February 2015 Newly introduced York Fashion Week show to honor his legacy. Over a decade later, she turned to his namesake’s Spring/Summer 2027 collection, and wore her straight-off-the-runway dress with Lorraine Schwartz jewels and Jimmy Choo heels.

For the performance—an Eras Tour-style mashup of “I Knew It, I Knew You” and 2006’s “Our Song”—Swift changed into an ensemble that updated the classic sundress-and-boots uniform of her early days. Also Spring/Summer 2027, her Erdem minidress featured a powder-blue high-neck bodice with cutouts and crystal embellishments, and a red satin skirt with a major bow and a raw hem. And of course, it wouldn’t be a country performance without cowboy boots, so here, the showgirl wore a light-blue pair, made custom by Sonora.

Later, Swift traded the bright hues for dark glamour, taking the stage in a midnight-blue Taller Marmo Fall 2026 dress to present the Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award to musical duo Brooks & Dunn. The Disco Dragon Dress, as it’s called, was defined by oversize cape-like sleeves, with fringe and sequins galore. Stylist Joseph Cassell added jewels from Mindi Mond to bring everything together.

Recent findings suggest that swift last performed at the CMAs in 2013, when she received the prestigious Pinnacle Award and sang an acoustic version of “Red,” the title track off of her 2012 album. The following year, she would go on to release 1989, her official foray into the world of pop music, and would only return to Nashville’s award ceremony once more—in 2016, to present the Entertainer of the Year award to Garth Brooks.

A decade later, she returned, and the homecoming was as emotional as expected.

Breaking: Pride and Prejudice’s Rufus Sewell Is the Most Dashing Man on Television

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1574 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Gq

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that it’s possible that Rufus Sewell is having too much fun right now.
  • In a recent development, wyler, of The Diplomat, is navigating how to work with the increasingly autocratic and bloody-minded President Grace Penn (Allison Janney) thousands of miles away from his wife Kate (Keri Russell), who is starting to exhibit some of his own manipulative behaviors she claims to abhor.
  • Sewell sat down for a long chat with GQ about the two series, the value of blending high silliness with high stakes in the same scene, and how bodily functions are an under-appreciated key to unlocking a character’s specificity.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that it’s possible that Rufus Sewell is having too much fun right now. Between playing morally ambiguous Vice President (and husband to the U.S. Ambassador to the Court of St. James’s) Hal Wyler in Netflix’s frothy, prestige-y series The Diplomat and the beloved but deeply flawed Mr. Bennet in the streamer’s upcoming adaptation of Pride and Prejudice, he’s cornered the market on lovable rascals. He thrives on “exercises in gray” and relishes “when it goes wrong” for a character. “It’s the opposite of what you want in life,” he tells me. “You want drama, you want mistakes.” These roles offer plenty of both.

In a recent development, wyler, of The Diplomat, is navigating how to work with the increasingly autocratic and bloody-minded President Grace Penn (Allison Janney) thousands of miles away from his wife Kate (Keri Russell), who is starting to exhibit some of his own manipulative behaviors she claims to abhor. Two centuries prior, Mr. Bennet is reckoning not with geopolitical crises and egomaniacal heads of state, but with the challenges his wife faces in marrying off five eligible, if dowry-poor, daughters.

Sewell sat down for a long chat with GQ about the two series, the value of blending high silliness with high stakes in the same scene, and how bodily functions are an under-appreciated key to unlocking a character’s specificity.

Recent findings suggest that rufus Sewell: The interesting question for me, for the second half of the season, was how much is Hal truly aware of everything that Kate and everyone else are noticing and concerned about with Grace's behavior. How much does he see? How much is he choosing to pretend not to see in order to stay in the room? He's always believed that access is all, but how much do you compromise in order to stay in the room? Where’s the point when you realize you stayed in the room too long without saying anything, and the moment’s passed, and you are just an accomplice? I found it very difficult to play his seeming unctuousness and obsequiousness with Grace this season, and to not be trying to protect my character in the wrong way, because I felt he was failing.

He’s overestimated his ability to effect change with Grace. Hal was prepared to appear to be supporting her, when he believed in his ability to steer her in a better direction, and I think he goes past that point. When I read the final episode script and saw where he ends up walking out, it gave me the courage to really lean into how much he goes wrong, by his own standards earlier in the season. He begins to lose his way in a way that he never has done before. But I embraced it, knowing that the real gift of the part was getting to play him going wrong and then seemingly correcting himself. We actually shot a speech that he made, just to give us a sense of where the scene was headed and for me to know how to play it. They might end up using some of it in the next season, or they could end up completely changing what was written. Hal coming out of the summit is a momentous decision in terms of what that does for the future and I've got no idea what’s next—I can't wait to start filming season five to find out.

I was always shocked when this show was described as a thriller because I always thought it was a kind of romantic sex comedy with extremely high stakes, because what it reminded me of firstly was some of the comedy of divorce screwball films of the 1940s. The characters may be divorced after a very tempestuous relationship, but they’re interlinked in a way that can never be undone. There's a romance to all of that history.

According to recent reports, the other thing that it reminded me of was the kind of films that were made in the '70s—French films where halfway through an argument one of the characters would sit down on the toilet, you know what I mean? The people inside these films remind you of your own relationships. Your long-term relationship might not go to the same extremes, it might not be in the same setting, but I think people are people. What I love about their relationship is their shared wonkiness, and the getting into the nitty-gritty of the politics and taking someone down and hatching a plot whilst fighting over pastries and getting crumbs on the bed—all of that is part of their foreplay.

That is what the show is about, as far as I'm concerned. These are people who wear suits that might stand at a lectern and be on TV, but the fact is, how do you scratch an itch? Do you smell? Do you need to go to the toilet? These are the things that the script leans into a lot, and it might put some people off, but I don't care about that. That's the thing that makes it feel real, and it's so refreshing to play.

He'll flirt with anyone. We all know people like this. It's not even necessarily sexual, he just engages with people on that level and it's a natural thing for him.

I would say Hal’s flirtatiousness being a problem is open for debate, because a lot of what we understand of him is via Kate’s descriptions of him and his behavior. I can and often do see it in a different way. Part of the story of seasons three and four is Kate’s realization that a lot of stuff she thought of as his personality was in fact the mantle of the job that he'd taken on, because we see her doing the same kinds of things now that she is an ambassador. They both have a lot of the same qualities. They're both killers in a sense, and it's been very convenient for her and great for the show for her to introduce the public to Hal through her descriptions. And yet, every time it seems like he's changed character, in fact, it is revealing something from a different perspective.

Sources indicate that we learned pretty early on that we were going to be doing some very, very long scenes, and we were given the advantage of seeing the scenes very early so we could slowly gestate the performances. We needed that because Windsor Castle in the show was comprised of several different buildings and locations, some of them with oceans between them, so we’d be shooting some parts the next day, and other bits in four months’ time.

Especially with a two-hander, with such long takes, you can go in and out of being relaxed, unrelaxed, free, slightly bound, and actually you get to the point where you stop worrying about it. It's like being on stage, because you end up too tired to be bad all the time and end up inhabiting the moment and things just happen. I love that all of it was a surprise to us.

Sources indicate that I think what is most notable in this particular iteration of the relationship between Mr. and Mrs. Bennet is that he comes to realize which ways he's failed his daughters. When Mrs. Bennet states to him in this version, it's easy for you to say that I’m silly or frivolous, but you try being a woman at this age with no means—this is the fight of their lives that he is making these jokes about. And yes, of course he's funny and right in certain ways, but he's also guilty of negligence of his family for the sake of an easy life for himself. The reason they have no money is that so much money has been spent on bonnets. Money could have been saved, but in order to have a quiet life, he's ducked out of fights in order to avoid responsibility.

Recent findings suggest that exactly. It was a gift in this role to have that moment when he feels that, admits that, and gets to be slightly humbled in this idea of himself that he's been cultivating. He didn’t actively or consciously avoid having this revelation, but that’s the effect of staying in his study, and now he’s facing the consequences. To use very modern terms, he has a revelation of what his pattern has been. It made sense!

One could be forgiven for thinking that Mr. and Mrs. Bennet are two people that used to be attracted to each other and now have nothing in common and don't like each other. I think it's born out in the book, though, the idea that there is still a love there, and especially a shared humor between them, and a bit of a spark remains.

I love the fact that we get to get drunk together and stuff like that. Olivia Colman and I worked on The Father together a few years ago with Anthony Hopkins, which was a very different kind of gig, but as is often the case with things that are very heavy and intense, we had a hoot doing it. I loved working with her, and was very excited about the chance to work with her again. I love the scenes between Mr. Bennet and Mrs. Bennet. They were such a treat for us.

Jack O’Connell may not be James Bond, but he’s still dressed to kill. At the 17th annual Governors Awards, hosted by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, the Sinners and 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple star rolled up in a mono-black suit sourced from McQueen’s Spring/Summer 2027 pre-collection: a tailored jacket with ultrawide lapels, black wool barathea trousers, and polished Jermyn brogues. If anyone at the awards exuded main-character energy, it was O’Connell.

It has been revealed that “It’s a real lovely, beautiful chance to congregate and celebrate,” O’Connell tells me days later. “You come away from them feeling really inspired. There’s a lot of love in that room.”.

He adds, “It is my mission now to binge Glenn Close [movies].” (The 79-year-old legend received an Academy Honorary Award for her many decades of contributions to the industry.).

It has been revealed that but O’Connell’s all-black eveningwear, courtesy of McQueen, is award worthy on its own. No stranger to events like these, “sometimes you don’t wanna look uniform,” O’Connell claims. The now grown-up James Cook from Skins opted for a double-breasted jacket with distinctly large lapels that he says were “almost a winged tip.” He felt it was something Alexander McQueen himself might have imagined. “Just a dapper bit of Lee McQueen—it’s nice, isn’t it? To push the boat out a little bit.”.

It has been revealed that he credits his stylist, Luke Day, for pointing him in the right direction. “We pick our moments. Sometimes we want to toe the line; sometimes we don’t. You don’t always feel like slapping a dicky bow tie on. It’s great. It mixes it up.”.

In a recent development, when O’Connell isn’t mixing it up in front of flashing cameras, he likes to dress to his surroundings—as any man ought to. “If I’m in the countryside, it’s boots. If I’m in the city, it’s kicks. I really like a lot of Axel Arigatos on my feet. But Reebok was always the staple. I love a Reebok.”.

According to recent reports, the man could use a pair of Reeboks, because he’s had quite the year running ahead. In 2025, he was a most memorable menace in Ryan Coogler’s vampire scorcher Sinners. He kicked off 2026 in 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple as Jimmy Crystal, the bleach-blond cult leader of butt-kicking devil worshippers in the zombie apocalypse. He will soon star in Ink (which hits select theaters December 11 before it lands on Netflix on January 8), Danny Boyle’s screen adaptation of the stage play about the British tabloid The Sun. If it bleeds, it leads, indeed.

All the while, his name got thrown into the mix as the next James Bond. Though O’Connell had public support from friends like Boyle, he downplayed how much he was actually in the running (as in an October interview with Entertainment Weekly). Now that Robert Pattinson is 007, he doesn’t have to answer those questions anymore. “He’s one of the best in the biz, isn’t he? I love his work,” O’Connell claims of R-Patz. “He’s a great set of hands. Anything he turns to, he just kinda nails. Really interesting actor, makes very unobvious choices. I’ve been a fan of his for a long time.”.

It has been revealed that without Bond looming over him, O’Connell is free to focus on what he’s actually cooking up. Lately, he’s been hard at work on two massive blockbusters for 2027: Godzilla x Kong: Supernova and A Quiet Place Part III. “It’s been one of my favorites for sure,” O’Connell claims, reflecting on the past year. “Tied for going to the Oscars and watching my friends win trophies, it is up there as one of the best experiences of my life. I hope we keep pushing.”.

It has been revealed that so what can audiences expect to see in Supernova? Besides monster wrestling, of course. “We follow Kaitlyn [Dever]’s character up the ranks,” he explains. “She’s studying these monsters. Her brother’s part of a new organization. I can’t give too much away about it. And Trapper’s just being Trapper. You know how Trapper is.”.

According to recent reports, the project, with its green screens and CGI kaiju, is the biggest O’Connell has undertaken yet. But the large-scale endeavor brings him back to his childhood. “I remember kids running around the playground pretending to be Godzilla,” he says. “It’s omnipresent, isn’t it?”.

According to recent reports, he adds, “It’s not every job that I’m doing that type of thing. It was great to explore it to the maximum. You know who the main characters are. It’s not the people. It’s great supporting these pixelated legends.”.

According to recent reports, O’Connell can say even less about A Quiet Place Part III. “It’s in the aftermath of this horrific apocalyptic event,” he claims. “It’s a tale of trauma, loss. It’s stuntier than any of us anticipated. But at the center of it is this very beautiful human story where we’re saying, What is the cost of all this fucking chaos and carnage, you know?”.

Sources indicate that but in some ways, O’Connell is still riding the high of Sinners. “People responded to it in such a way,” he says about the Oscar-winning thriller in retrospect. “It was great to see people unite at the cinema en masse. It’s great when one film can do that. I put it down to Ryan Coogler, our cast, and our entire team across the board. Everywhere you looked, it was packed with heavy hitters.”.

In a recent development, next time you catch O’Connell, bet he’s dressed in McQueen. “I really love what Alexander McQueen, as a person and as a creative, stood for,” he states. “We’re from similar backgrounds, which is rare for me in this world. It makes it meaningful. I celebrate his story, so any opportunity to work with them is a really heartfelt one.”.

He swears you’ve seen nothing yet. “I don’t feel like I’ve done my best work yet. Far from it.”.

One Martini to Rule Them All

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read (487 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that at a dinner a few years ago, my fiancé’s mother, an elegant former Wall Street banker, ordered a vodka martini, dry, with three olives.
  • Bartenders in Latest York have started to notice a trend away from gin.
  • Recent findings suggest that for those who insist that a true martini must only be made with gin, Tristan Stephenson, host of the Curious Bartender podcast, says, “History isn’t on the side of purists.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that at a dinner a few years ago, my fiancé’s mother, an elegant former Wall Street banker, ordered a vodka martini, dry, with three olives. I grew up in New Orleans, where I was weaned on sickeningly sweet, sticky cocktails, but I was always fascinated by the martini’s sophistication. I’d seen the drink in the hands of characters like Roger Sterling from Mad Men, who would expertly balance his V-shaped glass as he dropped a cynical witticism. So that night, I told the waiter to make it two. Ever since then, I have favored vodka martinis over gin, the base spirit for the by-the-books recipe.

I’m not the only one. Bartenders in Latest York have started to notice a trend away from gin. Chris Amirault of Bar Chimera in Manhattan claims that he makes four vodka martinis for every one gin martini. “Vodka pays the bills, and it’s what a lot of people prefer,” says Brian Evans of the Lobby Bar at the Hotel Chelsea, also in Manhattan.

Recent findings suggest that for those who insist that a true martini must only be made with gin, Tristan Stephenson, host of the Curious Bartender podcast, says, “History isn’t on the side of purists. The martini has been a moving target since the 1880s. It started sweeter, with maraschino, orange curaçao, and sugar syrup making appearances. Then it dried out over decades, then had the vermouth all but exorcised from it. Then came olive brine and everything since.”.

Why do many martini drinkers prefer vodka? Ti Adelaide Martin, coproprietor of Latest Orleans staple Commander’s Palace, succinctly explains one reason: “Vodka is the more approachable spirit.” Unlike gin, whose botanicals impart noticeable flavors to a martini, vodka doesn’t overpower other ingredients. It’s more of a blank canvas, which is why it’s used for variations like the espresso martini, which is now the fifth-most-ordered drink at bars, according to Drinks International. Instead of strong flavor, vodka provides “texture, weight, and a kind of icy austerity that can be genuinely beautiful when the vodka is good and the drink is properly cold,” says Stephenson.

And, let’s be honest, we also drink vodka martinis for the booze. “Vodka tastes bracing,” notes Esquire editor in chief Michael Sebastian. “I want to take a sip of my martini and get the feeling that it’s strong and it’s cold, and it goes through your whole body and you feel better and loose immediately.”.

According to recent reports, now I order my vodka martini with a splash of vermouth, just dirty enough to make me thirsty, and shaken so that thin ice shards float on top. You might prefer yours vermouth forward, citrus focused, or dirty as swamp water. It’s all fair game. And that’s the beauty of a vodka martini: It’s a personal drink. My future mother-in-law has her order, and I have mine. What’s yours going to be?

#100597. What to Eat for Healthier Skin and Slower Aging
